purpose: Authoritative machine-checkable inventory of high-confidence production placeholders, status drift, and narrow approved exception classes for the runtime-placeholder eradication initiative.

approved_exception_classes.description: Placeholder, stub, and TODO markers may appear in non-shipping test or fuzz surfaces when the marker does not leak into runtime code paths.
approved_exception_classes.closure_rule: Runtime code, manifests, and operator paths must not depend on these markers or import their behavior as a live fallback.

approved_exception_classes.description: Shared mock infrastructure may use placeholder-like naming as test scaffolding only when it stays inside dedicated mock or fixture crates.
approved_exception_classes.closure_rule: Approved mock infrastructure must remain outside live runtime, catalog, and connector shipping paths.

approved_exception_classes.description: Benchmark fixture helpers may use stub naming only for synthetic offline microbench input construction, not for user-facing benchmark results.
approved_exception_classes.closure_rule: User-facing `fwc bench` commands must report real measurements; only internal offline fixture builders may retain stub terminology.

approved_exception_classes.description: Offline schema or template emitters may carry placeholder sentinel values when runtime install and update paths reject demo markers and generator regression tests keep emitted runtime code truthful.
approved_exception_classes.closure_rule: Any placeholder sentinel in an offline generator must stay off runtime execution paths and remain covered by generator regression tests.

approved_exception_classes.description: Documentation and evidence artifacts may quote placeholder strings as part of audits, transcripts, or remediation records.
approved_exception_classes.closure_rule: Quoted placeholder markers in docs or evidence must remain descriptive only and must not be presented as live runtime capability.

findings.title: Tlon connector still ships as a planned-only scaffold
findings.rationale: The connector manifest remains `stub`, and the runtime self-description still advertises `planned_only` plus an unimplemented invoke path.
findings.exit_strategy: Graduate the connector to a truthful live or quarantined non-live state and remove planned-only runtime surfaces.
findings.verification_expectation: Connector-level unit and integration coverage plus catalog or status proofs that the connector no longer exposes a planned-only runtime contract.

findings.title: Hugging Face manifest and runtime status disagree
findings.rationale: The manifest still declares the connector as `stub` while handshake and introspection surfaces emit `surface_status = live` and expose live-request support.
findings.exit_strategy: Make manifest status, runtime handshake, introspection, and catalog truth converge on the same live or quarantined state.
findings.verification_expectation: Manifest or catalog consistency checks plus connector tests proving runtime and metadata status stay aligned.

findings.title: AWS connector still uses fake signing instead of SigV4
findings.rationale: Self-check and runtime messaging explicitly admit request signing is not implemented, and the client still sends raw `X-Aws-*` headers instead of canonical SigV4 signatures.
findings.exit_strategy: Adopt the shared SigV4 signer and replace the fake header path on real AWS requests.
findings.verification_expectation: Cross-cloud auth regression coverage plus connector verification proving real SigV4 request signing on the affected AWS surfaces.

findings.title: S3 presigned URLs still carry a placeholder signature
findings.rationale: The presign path still emits a literal `PLACEHOLDER_SIGNATURE` query component instead of a real SigV4 query signature.
findings.exit_strategy: Replace placeholder presigning with real SigV4 query signing backed by the shared canonical-request substrate.
findings.verification_expectation: Unit, integration, and connector-level verification that presigned URLs round-trip with real SigV4 query parameters.

findings.title: GCP service-account auth still refuses JWT bearer signing
findings.rationale: Service-account mode is explicitly rejected because JWT signing is not implemented yet, so the connector cannot truthfully support that auth path.
findings.exit_strategy: Implement JWT bearer signing and token exchange for service-account mode instead of hard-refusing the path.
findings.verification_expectation: Cross-cloud auth regression coverage plus connector-level tests proving service-account flows succeed and fail truthfully.

anchors.needle: GCP service_account mode requires JWT signing, which is not implemented yet.

findings.title: Bootstrap hardware-token flow is still stubbed and hard-fails
findings.rationale: Hardware-token discovery is still documented as a stub implementation, and the workflow returns `Hardware token support not yet fully implemented` instead of completing bootstrap.
findings.exit_strategy: Implement real PKCS#11-backed discovery and complete the hardware-token bootstrap path instead of hard-failing.
findings.verification_expectation: Hardware-token discovery and workflow tests, plus repeatable verification against a mock or soft-token path.

anchors.needle: This is a stub implementation - a real implementation would use the
Hardware token support not yet fully implemented

findings.title: Connector-state fork resolution still treats CRDT merge as a not-implemented placeholder
findings.rationale: Fork resolution records CRDT merge as a strategy but still fails with a not-implemented detector message rather than performing delta-level merge.
findings.exit_strategy: Implement real delta-level CRDT merge semantics for connector-state fork resolution.
findings.verification_expectation: Regression suites for fork resolution and CRDT merge semantics, including golden vectors or recovery scenarios.

anchors.needle: CRDT merge requires delta-level merging (not implemented in detector)

findings.title: Mesh planner zone filtering is still a no-op placeholder
findings.rationale: Placement planning still retains all candidates under zone restrictions because the planner lacks NodeInfo zone integration.
findings.exit_strategy: Plumb real node zone data into placement filtering and reject no-op zoning.
findings.verification_expectation: Zone-aware placement tests and diagnostics proving policy zone filters now change candidate selection truthfully.

findings.title: fwc intent still explains away missing log and lifecycle primitives
findings.rationale: The compiler still emits truthful but unresolved explanations for log tailing and lifecycle transitions because real host-backed primitives are missing.
findings.exit_strategy: Implement truthful host- or mesh-backed intent primitives so these verbs stop falling back to unsupported explanations.
findings.verification_expectation: Compiler and execution tests plus operator transcripts proving supported log and lifecycle intents map to real primitives.

anchors.needle: Connector log tailing is not implemented as a real `fwc` primitive yet.
That lifecycle transition is not implemented as a real `fwc` primitive because the host does not yet expose a truthful endpoint for it.

findings.title: fwc bench still mixes placeholder benchmark results into operator output
findings.rationale: User-facing benchmark subcommands still emit `BenchmarkResult::placeholder` results for connector activation, local invoke, mesh invoke, and secrets.
findings.exit_strategy: Replace placeholder benchmark branches with real harnesses, structured logs, and artifact capture.
findings.verification_expectation: Benchmark unit coverage, harness integration tests, and end-to-end scripts that capture stable artifacts and real measurements.

findings.title: fwc new still emits runtime placeholder operations and TODO-heavy limits
findings.rationale: The generator is a scaffold surface by design, but it still emits dead runtime placeholders instead of a truthful minimal viable connector baseline.
findings.exit_strategy: Redesign `fwc new` to emit truthful minimal viable connectors and then enforce that contract with generator regression tests.
findings.verification_expectation: Generator unit and smoke coverage proving emitted manifests and runtime code no longer contain dead placeholder operations or TODO-heavy runtime paths.

anchors.needle: TODO: Replace placeholders with the actual service limits before shipping.
